_comment: Phase 0 sweep definition. Each profile launches the server once with the given
flags, then runs every entry in `runs` against it. `wav` is resolved relative
The point of the sweep is to answer, with numbers rather than estimates:
- what latency does this GPU actually deliver, per model size and threshold
- how much VRAM SimulStreaming large-v3 really takes
- whether native FR->EN translation is meaningfully faster than NLLB
- whether one server can serve both the native and NLLB paths (see mixed-paths)

profiles.name: medium-simul
profiles.why: Baseline the 3070 can definitely run. If this sounds good enough, the VRAM question mostly goes away.

profiles.name: medium-simul-ft15
profiles.why: Same model, tighter AlignAtt lookahead. Measures what frame-threshold actually buys.

profiles.name: large-simul
profiles.why: The flagship configuration. Watch nvidia-smi while this runs - the VRAM figure is the point.

profiles.name: large-simul-ft15
profiles.why: Flagship model at the tighter threshold; the config most likely to ship.

profiles.name: large-fasterwhisper
profiles.why: The licence-clean fallback: CTranslate2 + LocalAgreement. Also ~3 GB instead of ~10.

profiles.name: native-en
profiles.why: FR->EN through Whisper's own translate task. Expect transcript-like latency and NO translation field.

profiles.name: nllb
profiles.why: EN->FR through NLLB. The sentence gate should show up as a much higher translation median than transcript median.

profiles.name: mixed-paths
profiles.why: THE open question: can one server serve the native FR->EN path AND the NLLB EN->FR path, or does flipping direction need a relaunch? If both runs below produce sane output, the UI never has to reload a model.

profiles.name: auto-lid
profiles.why: Bilingual source detection. Watch whether detected_language flips mid-stream on short utterances.
